method: Manual rubric: execute each prompt with Nexus enabled; score each assertion pass/fail/not-run with evidence. Compare against the same prompt without Nexus if benchmarking.

cases.expected_behavior: Ask for theme, audience and purpose; do not choose a site type.

cases.prompt: Use Nexus to build a developer portfolio using the supplied GitHub projects and profile.
cases.expected_behavior: Inspect provided source; clarify only missing essentials; create project-specific direction.

cases.prompt: Redesign an existing SaaS onboarding flow without changing its backend.
cases.expected_behavior: Preserve contracts, inspect code and design around activation.

cases.prompt: Build an immersive storefront for a ceramic studio with product variants.
cases.expected_behavior: Choose a signature rooted in ceramic materiality and implement scoped commerce functionality.

cases.prompt: Build an operations dashboard for incident triage with mock data.
cases.expected_behavior: Prioritize fast task completion and data legibility; label mocks.

cases.prompt: Create an online journal with long essays and photographs.
cases.expected_behavior: Prioritize reading, typographic rhythm and editorial hierarchy.
assertions: No product card grid by default

cases.prompt: Build a narrative site in which a model travels between sections and can be rotated.
cases.expected_behavior: Specify real geometry/projection, anchors, transitions, picking and fallback when justified.

cases.prompt: Use Nexus to write a production-ready spec for an architecture studio. Do not code.
cases.expected_behavior: Deliver concrete project-specific specification without implementation.

cases.prompt: Use Nexus to fix a tiny typo in a website footer.
cases.expected_behavior: Honor narrow scope rather than launching an unnecessary creative overhaul.

cases.prompt: Build the experience but assume no browser is available.
cases.expected_behavior: Implement as far as tools permit and report unrun browser tests.
